Subject: Post-call recap & caching assumptions (Opsly)

Thanks Jordan & Priya — great call earlier. Quick recap and action items so we’re aligned on pricing inputs and cache assumptions for the commercial model.

Key takeaways:
- Opsly is targeting a rollout to ~1.2M MAUs (phase 1) with heavy usage in the dashboard flows and notifications.
- Typical usage profile from the call: ~3 prompts/user/day on average, avg ~75 tokens/prompt (range 40-150).
- Opsly wants predictable unit economics and a target effective price in the range of $6–$9 per 1M billable tokens for the initial contract.

Caching assumptions I took away & what we used in the attached model (cache_modeling_v1.xlsx):
1) Prefix/template cache: ~40% hit rate for templated prompts (dashboard notifications, canned responses). This is based on similar customers where a small set of high-frequency templates dominate traffic.
2) Session/KV cache: we modeled an additional ~10–15% effective token reduction from KV cache reuse across multi-turn flows.
3) Overall modeled hit rate: 45–55% range in the spreadsheet (conservative / expected / aggressive tabs).

Effect on effective $/1M tokens (example):
- List price (example) = $12 / 1M raw tokens.
- If raw tokens = 50M/month and cache hit rate = 50% -> billable tokens = 25M.
- Effective price = (list_price * raw_tokens) / billable_tokens = ($12 * 50M) / 25M = $24 / 1M billable tokens equivalent.
  Note: That calculation treats "list_price" as the cost per raw token; for commercial quoting we typically convert to an "effective $/1M billable tokens" to compare against customer targets.

Two important notes:
- Hit rates matter more for unit economics than raw volume — a 10 percentage-point improvement in cache hit can materially reduce monthly cost.
- We need a representative prompt sample (1–2k prompts) from you so Aditya (solutions engineering) can run the cacheability analysis and give a more confident hit-rate estimate.

Next steps / asks:
- Jordan / Priya: share a anonymized sample of prompts or a small export (1–2k rows) by EOD 7/15.
- I’ll loop in Aditya (SE) to run cache modeling and produce a refined hit-rate and effective $/1M tokens by 7/18.
- We’ll follow with a draft commercial proposal (SOW + price bands) by 7/22.

Attachments: cache_modeling_v1.xlsx (initial assumptions & scenarios), proposal-OPS-4721.pdf (placeholder).

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and the numbers you asked for:

Quick numbers (current estimate):
- Monthly active users (phase 1): ~1.2M
- Avg prompts / user / day: ~3 (spiky during peak hours)
- Avg tokens / prompt: 75 (we have a distribution — some auto-generated notifications ~30 tokens, some long-form summaries ~200 tokens)
- Typical monthly raw tokens (estimate): ~1.2M users * 3 prompts/day * 75 tokens * 30 days ≈ 8.1B raw tokens/month (this is our back-of-envelope; we want to refine).
- Opsly budget range we’re targeting (total cloud/LLM spend): $75k–$150k / month initially. We want to understand how Redwood’s effective $/1M billable tokens maps to that budget.

About cache hit rates — from our side:
- For templated notifications and dashboard snippets we’ve seen ~40% cache hit historically (same notification payloads).
- Session-based reuse (same user asking follow-ups) gives another ~10% on top in some flows.

We’ll pull a representative sample and scrub PII. Priya will send a 2k-row sample by 7/15. Can you confirm: in your model are cached tokens fully non-billable, or do you model a small partial charge for cached prefixes? Also want to see the sensitivity table for 35%/45%/60% hit rates.

— Jordan

- Sensitivity: the spreadsheet includes 35% / 45% / 60% overall hit-rate tabs. We’ll run your sample through the model to populate the realistic expected hit range.
